applies_why: The judge breaks the challenger's link using Matthew 1:18 and 1:25, which is exactly the act the rule's final sentence governs.
quote: CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN -- [L1] Matthew 1:18 "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost" and Matthew 1:25 "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son" contradict C3's claim of espousal union
rule_words: counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge uses to break a link is counted this way.
room: "A verse the judge uses to break a link is counted this way": reading one, a breaking verse counts only if the judge quotes the earlier-round sentence that pressed it against that link and names that round; reading two, it merely tallies breaking verses without imposing that condition; reading one governs because "counted this way" points back to the whole "only when" condition.
why: The judge broke the challenger's link with Matthew 1:18 and 1:25 while quoting only the Bible text itself, never quoting an earlier round's sentence that pressed those verses against the link and never naming any round, so under the rule those verses cannot count.
